sections.title: Motivation, overview and history
sections.extract: The outstanding mathematician Wilhelm Magnus (1907-1990) made important contributions to a wide variety of fields in mathematics and mathematical physics [1]. Among them, one can mention combinatorial group theory [2] and his collaboration in the Bateman project on higher transcendental functions and integral transforms [3]. sections.title: Physical applications
sections.extract: From previous sections it should be clear that ME has a strong bearing on both Classical and Quantum Mechanics. As far as Classical Mechanics is concerned, this has been most explicitly shown in Section 3.4. On its turn Quantum Mechanics has been repeatedly invoked as a source of applications, among others, in Sections 2.9 and 4. sections.title: Nuclear, atomic and molecular physics
sections.extract: As far as we know, the first physical application of ME dates back to 1963. Robinson [18] published a brand new formalism to investigate multiple Coulomb excitations of deformed nuclei. As a matter of fact, he states explicitly that only after completion of his work did he discover the ME. His derivation of ME formulas is certainly worth reading. sections.extract: This is certainly the field where ME has been most systematically used and so we consider it separately. sections.title: Conclusions
sections.extract: In this report, we have thoroughly reviewed the abiding work on Magnus expansion carried out over more than fifty years, from very different perspectives.
